etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English oppressen, from Old French oppresser, from Medieval Latin oppressare (“to press against, oppress”), frequentative of Latin opprimere, past participle oppressus (“to press against, press together, oppress”), from ob (“against”) + premere, past participle pressus (“to press”); see press.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To keep down by unjust force.
(transitive, obsolete) Physically to press down on (someone) with harmful effects; to smother, crush.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book II, Canto X”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: Most mercilesse of women, VVyden hight, / Her other sonne fast sleeping did oppresse, / And with most cruell hand him murdred pittilesse.

definitions.definition: (transitive, obsolete) To sexually violate; to rape.
